turns.text: 5:57 am update, typing one-handed sorry. my son Theo is 6 weeks old and i am already dreading the witching hour tonight. wife is resting so it's on me today. can you put together a feeding and soothing plan for the late afternoon and evening in table form? the crying usually starts around 5 and goes until about 8, so i want it timed around that. please and thanks

Happy to. Here's a plan built around a 5-8 p.m. crying stretch. I'm assuming feeds about every 2.5-3 hours at his age, so adjust to his usual rhythm.

| Time | What | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 3:00-3:30 | Last nap wrap-up, then a full feed | Aim for a calm, full bottle so he isn't hungry going in |
| 3:30-4:30 | Awake time: light play, tummy time, a short stroller walk | Fresh air and motion can help before the fussy window |
| 4:30 | Prep: dim lights, white noise on, bottle warmed and within reach, burp cloths, swaddle ready | Do your own setup so you aren't scrambling mid-cry |
| 5:00-5:45 | First wave: hold upright, slow bouncing or swaying, white noise, shushing | Check the basics first: diaper, gas, temperature |
| 5:45-6:00 | Small top-up feed (about half a normal bottle) | Cluster feeding is common in the evening; offer smaller amounts and burp well |
| 6:00-7:00 | Rotate: carrier walk, side-lying hold, warm bath if he likes it | Switch methods every 10-15 minutes, since nothing works forever |
| 7:00-7:30 | Dim everything, quiet voice, swaddle, rock | Wind-down cues |
| 7:30-8:00 | Final feed, burp, then down for the night | Crying often tapers off around here |

A few things to keep in mind: take a 5-minute break if you feel frazzled (put him safely in his crib and step away), and ask your wife to take over once she's rested so you get a breather too. If crying is inconsolable for hours, he has a fever, or feeds are being refused, call the pediatrician.

Is there anything that already calms him that I should build in?

yes actually, humming a slowed-down ballpark organ tune is the only thing that reliably calms him. should i build that into the routine? also i'm researching formula options because i think the store-brand powder we use is making him fussy. we see the pediatrician tomorrow so i'm gonna ask

Yes, build it in. A consistent, familiar sound is a great soothing cue. Here's how I'd use it:

- **5:00-5:45 first wave:** start humming it low and slow while swaying, rather than saving it as a last resort.
- **6:00-7:00 rotation:** hum during the carrier walk and the bath, so it pairs with every method.
- **7:00-7:30 wind-down:** hum it softer and slower each time through, and let it fade out as he gets drowsy. Over days it becomes a sleep cue too.

Save a few full rounds for the hardest moments so it still feels special to him.

On formula, asking tomorrow is the right move. Don't switch on your own tonight, since changing formula abruptly can cause its own fussiness and you'd lose a clean comparison. Questions to bring:

| Question | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| Could the fussiness be gas, reflux, or a protein sensitivity? | Each points to different fixes |
| Would a gentle or partially hydrolyzed formula be worth trying? | A common first step for fussiness |
| How long should a trial last? | Usually 1-2 weeks to judge |
| Are there signs that mean it's more urgent? | Blood in stool, poor weight gain, vomiting |

Bring a note of when the crying starts and ends, how much he's eating, and any patterns. That makes the visit more productive. You've got a solid plan for tonight, so good luck.
